metadata.title: Trigger CD Pipeline
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Trigger the CD/release pipeline using configuration loaded in the previous step. Unlike CI (which is auto-triggered by push), CD must be actively triggered via the ADO API. Passes source branch and environment parameters to the pipeline run.

output.description: CD pipeline run ID and trigger status

prerequisites: Load Deploy Config step completed (deployConfig with cd section in memory)
CD pipeline definition exists and is accessible in ADO
specificActions: Determine source branch: use cd.source_branch if set, otherwise detect current git branch
Trigger the CD pipeline via mcp__azuredevops__pipelines_run with pipeline_definition_id and source branch
Pass target_environments as pipeline parameters if supported
Record the returned run ID in memory as cdPipelineRunId
Handle trigger failures: API errors, permission issues, pipeline not found
If trigger fails, store error details and set cdTriggerStatus to 'failed'
tools: Bash - git branch detection (current branch name)
mcp__azuredevops__pipelines_run - Trigger the CD pipeline run
bestPractices: Always read config from memory — never re-read the config file in this step
Use the current git branch unless cd.source_branch explicitly overrides it
Verify the pipeline trigger was accepted before proceeding (check for a valid run ID)
Log the full trigger request details for debugging if the trigger fails
Distinguish between transient trigger failures (network, timeout) and permanent ones (permission, not found)
Key difference from CI: CI is auto-triggered by push, CD must be actively triggered via API

substeps.name: Get Pipeline Config from Memory
substeps.description: Retrieve the resolved CD pipeline configuration
actions: Read deployConfig from memory
Extract cd.pipeline_definition_id, cd.target_environments, cd.source_branch
Verify ado_project and pipeline_definition_id are present

substeps.name: Determine Source Branch
substeps.description: Resolve which branch to deploy from
actions: If cd.source_branch is set, use it as the source branch
Otherwise, detect the current git branch via Bash (git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
Record the resolved source branch for the trigger call

substeps.name: Trigger CD Pipeline
substeps.description: Execute the pipeline run via ADO API
actions: Call mcp__azuredevops__pipelines_run with:
- project: deployConfig.ado_project
- pipeline definition ID: deployConfig.cd.pipeline_definition_id
- source branch: resolved branch from substep 1
- parameters: target_environments if pipeline supports parameterized environments
Record the returned run ID

substeps.name: Record Run ID and Status
substeps.description: Store the pipeline run information in memory
actions: Store cdPipelineRunId in memory
Set cdTriggerStatus to 'triggered' on success
Record trigger timestamp for timeout tracking

substeps.name: Handle Trigger Failures
substeps.description: Handle cases where the pipeline trigger fails
actions: Only execute if the trigger call failed
Capture error details: API error message, HTTP status, permission issues
Set cdTriggerStatus to 'failed'
Store error details for the evaluate-deployment-result step to process
Distinguish between: pipeline not found, permission denied, invalid parameters, network error

substeps.name: End-Step: Compliance Check
actions: Output: '✓ Step completed in compliance with operating principles'

flow.description: Get config from memory → Determine source branch → Trigger CD pipeline via API → Record run ID → Handle failures (if any)

memoryFileUsage.readFrom: Deploy config (deployConfig with cd section from load-deploy-config step)
fields: Information Produced: cdPipelineRunId (ADO pipeline run ID), cdTriggerStatus (triggered/failed)
Decisions Made: Source branch selection (config override vs current branch), trigger parameters
